rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2014> a two-year (2008-2009) field experiment at E<U+011F>irdir Fruit Growing Research Station, Isparta, Turkey, comparing flood irrigation (control) with eight drip irrigation schedules (two intervals x four pan coefficients) on Starkrimson Delicious apple, with own measurements of fruit quality and shoot growth (Tables 3-9).
rows.notes: The study is a primary field trial on the conversion from flood to drip irrigation in an apple orchard, but it does not measure or report yield (kg per tree or per ha). Its own results concern fruit quality (fruit diameter, length, weight per fruit, flesh firmness, soluble solids, colour, size-class ratios) and vegetative growth (shoot number, length, diameter). The Results and Conclusion state that drip irrigation gave larger fruit and higher extra/class-1 ratios than flood irrigation and better shoot growth, but no yield figure is given, so it provides no own evidence that drip adoption increased yield as the passage claims. Individual fruit weight and size are yield components, which may be why the review attributes a yield increase to it, but this is not a yield result. Note also that the drip and flood treatments differed in irrigation interval and first-irrigation date (drip started 20-21 May, flood 24-27 June), and the ANOVA only reports Duncan letter groupings without dispersion measures.

notes: Full text appears complete except for abstract, highlights, keywords, tables and references being absent; the text is a two-year single-site field experiment (clay loam soil, one apple cultivar) with three replications.
